problem: RL-based visual navigation agents assume static environments, but in cluttered scenes interactable obstacles (shoes, boxes) make the environment non-stationary, and recurrent policies struggle to decide whether to push obstacles when finding the next waypoint.
motivation: Real cluttered homes contain movable objects blocking the path, so agents must use historical interaction information to decide when to interact. Transformer encoders capture spatial-temporal dependencies well, but training them directly in RL is unstable.
key_idea: Replace the recurrent memory in an interactive-navigation RL policy with a transformer-based memory over history, stabilized by an auxiliary next-waypoint prediction objective.
insight: The abstract says the auxiliary next-waypoint prediction task facilitates representation learning and bootstraps RL, making transformer memory trainable. It claims gains over the Interactive Gibson benchmark and a recurrent RL policy on both seen and unseen scenes. Only the abstract was available, so no ablation details can be cited.
method: POMDP formulation: casts interactive visual navigation with movable obstacles as a partially observed MDP.
Transformer memory: a transformer encoder over historical observations/interaction information replaces the recurrent state in the RL policy.
Auxiliary surrogate objective: predicts the next waypoint as an auxiliary task to aid representation learning and stabilize RL training.

setting.backbone: Transformer-encoder memory policy trained with RL (details not available)
setting.training_data: RL in iGibson / Interactive Gibson scenes (scale not stated in abstract)
setting.observation: egocentric visual observations (details not stated in abstract)

results: The abstract claims significant improvements over the Interactive Gibson benchmark and a recurrent RL policy, in both validation-seen and test-unseen scenes. No numbers are given.
limitations: Only the abstract was available, so quantitative results and ablations are unknown.
Evaluation appears limited to simulation (iGibson), with no real-robot experiments mentioned.
